title: QBR risk triage and conversation map template
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight QBR agenda + facilitation guide focused on rapid renewal risk triage and action-oriented conversation mapping. Use for mid-market accounts where renewal signals are mixed and we need a single meeting to align on top priorities, owners, and measurable next steps.

Intended audience:
- CS lead (you)
- Executive sponsor (customer)
- Product/PM cadence owner
- Technical contact / eng lead (customer)
- Finance or procurement (if procurement is active)

Before the meeting (pre-read & checklist, to send 4 business days out):
- Send 1-page pre-read: current usage + 90d trend + top 3 risks + proposed mitigations (attach 1 slide).
- Confirm attendees and objective: "Align on renewal posture and agree on top 3 actions with owners."
- Internal prep: quick risk score (RAG) in CRM + 1-sentence rationale per risk. Link CRM card.
- If technical risk flagged, have SRE/solutions backup on standby.
- Prepare ask: budget/commitment ask or next-step proposal (e.g., pilot expansion, PO cadence).
- Attach one-line success metrics we will track post-QBR.

Meeting length and timeboxing (60 minutes recommended):
- 0–5m: Quick intros & objective slide (CS lead). Set the rule: "This is a working session to identify concrete owners and timelines."
- 5–15m: Health snapshot (CS lead). Usage, adoption, latency/ops incidents, ROI signals. Keep slides to 2 bullets each.
- 15–30m: Customer perspective (customer exec + tech). Ask: what would success look like in 90 days? What keeps you up at night?
- 30–45m: Risk triage (facilitated). Walk through red/amber/green triggers and map owners. Use conversation map.
- 45–55m: Action commitment & timeline (SWIM lanes). Assign owners, due dates, and success metric for each action.
- 55–60m: Close & confirm follow-up (CS lead). Confirm single follow-up owner and date.

Conversation map (scripted prompts by stakeholder):
- Exec sponsor level (5–7 mins):
  - "From your perspective, is the investment meeting your org's priorities? If not, which priorities are pulling budget?"
  - "If we could fix one thing in the next 60 days that would make renewal a clear yes, what would it be?"
  - Watch for: procurement timelines, headcount changes, exec churn.
- Product/PM:
  - "Are there upcoming product roadblocks or roadmap dependencies that affect the integration?"
  - "Which feature gaps are preventing broader adoption?"
- Technical/Eng contact:
  - "Any unresolved incidents or performance issues that still require engineering time?"
  - "Do you have telemetry gaps we should prioritize to prove ROI?"
- Finance/Procurement (if present):
  - "What internal approvals are needed and what are the gating dates?"
  - "Are there contract/PO items we should prepare ahead of vendor review?"

Risk taxonomy & red/amber/green triggers (use to score before meeting):
- Green (low risk): stable usage + no exec churn, contract on track, positive ROI evidence. Trigger examples: 7%+ monthly usage growth, NPS > 8 from power users.
- Amber (medium risk): plateauing usage, minor technical debt, procurement prep not started. Trigger examples: <3% MoM growth, 1-2 unresolved P1/P2 incidents in past 90d.
- Red (high risk): exec sponsor changed or disengaged, procurement delays >30d, active outages impacting core flows. Trigger examples: sponsor left in last 90d, finance paused renewals, negative ROI cited in stakeholder emails.

Facilitation playbook & short scripts (language to use):
- When surfacing a risk: "We want to surface this now so we can prioritize a short list of concrete actions — it helps us avoid surprises in 30 days."
- When asking for a commitment: "Can you confirm who will own X and a realistic date for delivery? We will add this as a tracked milestone and send a one-line weekly update."
- When customer is defensive: mirror + reframe: "I hear that the integration has been resource-constrained. If we could offload the initial telemetry work, would that move the needle for you?"

Common red flags to call out (quick checklist):
- Exec sponsor missed 2+ QBRs or declined invite
- Finance/Procurement silence after proposal sent
- Multiple critical incidents in the quarter without remediation plan
- Top customers at a feature parity gap with competitors
- Adoption limited to 1–2 teams with no expansion plan

Action commitment template (one-liner per action):
- Action: "Install prefix caching config in staging"
- Owner: "Eng lead — Maria"
- Due: "2026-03-15"
- Success metric: "Cache hit rate > 60% on targeted routes"
- Follow-up cadence: "CS weekly status note every Tue"

Post-meeting deliverables (to send within 48 hours):
- 1-paragraph meeting summary (who attended, top 3 risks, 3 committed actions with owners + due dates). Keep to 6 bullet lines.
- Shared milestone board link (or spreadsheet).
- Add tasks to customer Success Jira with tags: qbr, renewal-risk, <customer-name>.
- Schedule 15-min sync 2 weeks out to check progress on at-risk items.

Escalation path (if action owner misses deliverable):
- Day 3 after missed due date: CS lead pings owner for update (Slack + 1-line status).
- Day 7: escalate to customer exec sponsor with status note and ask for help prioritizing.
- Day 14: internal exec alert (CS manager + AE) and propose contingency (e.g., trial extension, interim credits).

Sample subject lines & Slack snippets:
- Email subject (post-QBR): "QBR recap + 3 actions — Acme Corp — due 2026-03-15"
- Slack DM to owner: "Quick check: are we on track to finish X by 3/15? I can help coordinate if you need support."

Slide deck outline (2–6 slides max):
1) Cover & objective (1 line objective)
2) Health snapshot (usage, incidents, ROI bullets)
3) Customer perspective & success criteria (3 bullets from customer)
4) Risk triage (RAG + top 3 risks and proposed mitigations)
5) Action commitments (table of owner/due/success metric)
6) Close & next steps (owner + check-in date)

Notes to self / draft thoughts (choppy, keep):
- Try a "pre-commit" process: ask for a 15-min internal alignment with AE and engineering 48h before QBR to avoid surprises.
- Consider a templated milestone sheet per account so follow-ups are always in same place.
- Might make sense to add a simple quantitative "renewal likelihood" score (0–10) in CRM to track trend across QBRs.

Unresolved questions:
- Should we require the customer to send a 1-paragraph current-state note before the meeting? Pros: surfaces issues; cons: reduces attendance.
- Do we escalate to legal for procurement delays longer than 45 days? Check with legal on auto-escalation SOP.

References and docs to copy into customer-facing template:
- Link to Confluence QBR Templates Master (see linked_artifacts).
- Example Jira tasks: CS-870 (renewal milestone board), CON-1342 (contract template updates).

Versioning & ownership:
- Template owner: Aisha Patel (CS enablement).
- Suggested review cadence: quarterly (sync with AE and Solutions).

If you use this template, please add quick feedback line to the Confluence page (one-liner: what changed / what didn't work).
